summary: John's 5th great-grandfather; seigneurial gamekeeper (herrschaftlicher Jäger) of the Kageneck lordship at Munzingen, probably a son of the Ibental Kageneck gamekeeper Jakob Heitzler.
bio: Joseph Heizler was the 'herrschaftlicher Jäger' — seigneurial gamekeeper of the Counts of Kageneck, lords of Munzingen (Schloss 1672) and from 1702 of Stegen and the Ibental. He married M. Anna Federer of Munzingen there on 26 Dec 1799 (FamilySearch tree event). Children include Friedrich (b. 8 Mar 1809), Agatha (b. 26 Jun 1813) and Veronica (d. 29 Apr 1815 of measles, aged about 1½, 'Tochter des Joseph Heizler'; witness Johann Federer) — so he was alive and living in Munzingen in 1815. He had died by 7 Oct 1835 ('+ Josef Heizler, gewesenen herrschaftlichen Jägers'). The tree gives 1773–1825 and makes him son of Jacob Heitzler and Catharina Begelspacher. Round 1 found no Joseph among Jakob's recorded children (Andreas 1764, Agathe 1771, Franziska 1779, Jakob 1781), but the gaps (1765–70, 1772–78) leave room for a Joseph b. c.1773; a Kageneck gamekeeper's son serving as the Kagenecks' gamekeeper at their Munzingen seat fits well, so the link is Probable (upgraded in round 3). He is not the Ibental teacher Joseph Heitzler (1765–1828) nor the Wehrlehof Joseph — the deep-dive warned the tree may have merged two Josephs. His Munzingen death entry (1815–35) would give his age and perhaps birthplace; the 1816–31 deaths are running text and were not finished.
